findings.description: The RDS instance sets publicly_accessible = true, giving it a public IP and exposing the MySQL endpoint to the internet, where it can be reached by anyone who can pass the security group rules or who discovers the endpoint.
storage_encrypted = false means the database volume and its snapshots are stored unencrypted, so anyone with access to the underlying storage or a copied snapshot can read the data.

The master password is supplied from var.password (a plain Terraform variable, stored in state in cleartext) and the master username is the predictable 'admin'. Combined with public accessibility this makes credential compromise and brute forcing much easier.

findings.issue_category: missing IAM authentication and audit logging
findings.description: No IAM database authentication, no enabled_cloudwatch_logs_exports (audit/error logs), and no KMS key are configured, so database access relies solely on a static password and leaves no auditable record of access.

The EC2 user_data embeds the RDS master username and password in cleartext. Instance user_data is retrievable from the unauthenticated-to-the-instance IMDS endpoint (and via ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute), leaking the database master credentials to any process or SSRF on the host.

No metadata_options block requiring http_tokens = "required" is set, so IMDSv1 remains enabled. An SSRF in the PHP app could retrieve the instance profile credentials (which hold s3:*, ec2:*, rds:*) and the secret-bearing user_data.
No root_block_device with encrypted = true is specified, so the instance's volume — which contains the dbinfo.inc file holding the database password — is stored unencrypted.

The instance role grants s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* on Resource "*". Compromise of the web server yields full control over all S3 buckets, EC2 infrastructure, and RDS databases in the account, including snapshot exfiltration and instance creation.
The database security group allows all outbound traffic to 0.0.0.0/0 on every protocol and port, enabling data exfiltration or command-and-control communication from a compromised database host.

findings.issue_category: TLS not enforced for database connections
findings.description: The MySQL parameter group does not set require_secure_transport = 1, so the publicly accessible database accepts unencrypted client connections and credentials/data can be intercepted in transit.

The database security group permits MySQL port 3306 from the entire VPC CIDR rather than only from the application instance's security group, so any workload in the VPC can reach the database directly.
